title: The quantum supremum of the $I_{3322}$ Bell inequality is not attained in finite dimension
abstract: In 2010, Pál and Vértesi found a family of finite-dimensional strategies for the $I_{3322}$ Bell inequality whose optimized values appeared to converge as the local Hilbert-space dimension grew. They conjectured that this limit is the supremum over all finite-dimensional quantum strategies, but that no finite-dimensional strategy attains it. We prove both claims. The proof uses the symmetry of the Bell functional to associate every strategy with a finite matrix of probabilities, one for each pair of spectral subspaces of Alice and Bob. This matrix gives an upper bound on the Bell value, and finite-dimensional strategies built from the repeating structure found by Pál and Vértesi approach it as the dimension grows. If the bound were attained exactly in finite dimension, the optimality conditions would then require a state that cannot be normalized. Consequently, the set of finite-dimensional quantum correlations is not closed in the $(3,3,2,2)$ scenario, the smallest Bell scenario where this can happen. Moreover, approaching the supremum requires unbounded local dimension. The core of the proof was formalized in Lean~4.
summary: This theoretical work proves that the quantum supremum of the $I_{3322}$ Bell inequality cannot be reached using any finite-dimensional quantum strategy. The authors show that while the supremum is approached by a specific sequence of strategies, achieving it requires an infinitely large local dimension. This highlights a non-closure property for quantum correlations in this specific scenario.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the quantum supremum of the $I_{3322}$ Bell inequality can be attained using strategies restricted to finite local Hilbert space dimensions.
main_result: The authors prove that the quantum supremum is approached by a specific family of strategies (Pál–Vértesi) but is never actually attained in any finite dimension.
method: The proof uses symmetry arguments on the Bell functional, mapping strategies to finite probability matrices, and employing contradiction to show that optimality requires an unnormalizable state.
model_or_system: The system is defined by the $I_{3322}$ Bell inequality, which is a specific quantum correlation test involving four measurement settings (3, 3, 2, 2). The analysis focuses on the limitations imposed by finite local dimensions.
key_observables: The Bell value $I_{3322}$, the supremum $ eta_{PV}$, and the upper-bound functional $\Phi(	heta)$ derived from spectral-weight matrices.
important_parameters: The local Hilbert-space dimension ($n$), which must be unbounded to approach the supremum.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on reducing the Bell value to an upper bound $\Phi(	heta)$ dependent on the spectral-weight matrix $	heta$, and formalizing the proof in Lean 4.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the Pál–Vértesi construction pattern for measurements, and Figure 2 shows how the spectral-weight matrix entries are reproduced by the PV chains.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the equality between the quantum supremum and the limit derived from the PV family, then uses contradiction based on optimality conditions to prove non-attainment in finite dimensions, concluding that the set of finite-dimensional correlations is not closed.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous mathematical boundary on the correlations achievable in quantum information protocols, demonstrating a fundamental gap between the supremum and any finite-dimensional realization.
